🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-10-09 23:00 → 2026-10-10 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Mode 4 r3 preflight halted cleanly at the spec boundary** — all twelve checksum entries verified and SPECIFICATION_INCOMPLETE flagged before any implementation step, confirming spec-first discipline held. [tg:tawg:5402]

> **Optimistic JCS hash challenge built, benchmarked, and committed to the ERC-8373 spec doc** — a prototype idea became reference implementation documentation inside a single window. [tg:tawg:5407]

> **Duplicate-id case elevates r4 from normative wrap-up to behavior correction** — what initially looked like a routine follow-on to r3 now addresses a concrete behavioral discrepancy. [tg:tawg:5405]

> **Agent Service Order Amendments pre-ERC posted to Ethereum Magicians** — a new framework for mutually agreed mid-execution changes to bounded agent actions entered public forum discussion. [ERC-8312 Magicians post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8312-bounded-agent-actions/28851/75)

## 🤝 **What moved**

### erc-8373 / Mode 4 preflight

_The r3 preflight reached a clean, honest checkpoint and r4 scope gained early clarity._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Completed** the code-disjoint Mode 4 r3 preflight, verified all twelve SHA256SUMS entries, and stopped correctly at SPECIFICATION_INCOMPLETE before any implementation work — giving the group a trustworthy boundary and a clean handoff point for the next revision. [tg:tawg:5402]

- Merlini (@gobross) **Validated** that halting at SPECIFICATION_INCOMPLETE rather than proceeding speculatively was exactly the right call, and confirmed the concrete case under review; this peer check closes the preflight loop and aligns the group on scope before r4 work begins. [tg:tawg:5404]

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Identified** that the duplicate-id case materially changes r4 from a normative wrap-up into a real behavior correction, giving the group accurate scope expectations well before review rather than letting the gap surface mid-cycle. [tg:tawg:5405]

### erc-8373 / optimistic-jcs

_The optimistic JCS hash challenge moved from suggestion through implementation to spec documentation._

- Baby Blue Viper **Built** the hash-based challenge proposed by Jimmy and measured it across five ERC-8373 statements from the recompute-kit, converting a discussion idea into reproducible benchmark data that justifies the optimistic anchor design. [tg:tawg:5386]

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Confirmed** Baby Blue Viper's implementation as complete and fully functional, providing the expert review that moves the optimistic approach from experimental to validated and clears the path for spec-level documentation. [tg:tawg:5406]

- Baby Blue Viper **Anchored** the work in the spec with commit a397f72f on TMerlini/ERCs#2, adding a paragraph to the ERC-8373 Reference Implementation section that names both OptimisticJcsAnchor and PinpointJcsAnchor and links the repository, making the implementation discoverable to future reviewers. [tg:tawg:5407]

### erc-8312

_A new pre-ERC proposal for agent service order amendments entered public forum discussion._

- **Shared** a pre-ERC proposal for Agent Service Order Amendments — a mechanism for mutually agreed changes to in-flight bounded agent actions — opening an Ethereum Magicians thread where the broader community can engage the design early. [ERC-8312 Magicians post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8312-bounded-agent-actions/28851/75)

### agent-evidence-atlas

_Cross-reference outreach connected ERC-8373 implementation expertise to a new labeling effort._

- Petchevere (@petchevere) **Tagged** Baby Blue Viper in probityai/agent-evidence-atlas#53 as a candidate reader for the execution-join-ref vector set, bridging active ERC-8373 implementation knowledge to a related evidence-labeling effort at a moment when that expertise matters most. [tg:tawg:5408]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- Does the duplicate-id behavior correction in r4 depend on the SPECIFICATION_INCOMPLETE boundary from r3, or can each be addressed independently?
- PinpointJcsAnchor is now named in the spec — does it warrant the same reference narrative treatment as OptimisticJcsAnchor?
- The ERC-8312 Ethereum Magicians thread is fresh — early TAWG engagement could shape the bounded-agent-action scope.

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Review the execution-join-ref vector set in agent-evidence-atlas#53 — Baby Blue Viper has been tagged as a candidate reader.
- Scope r4 to explicitly include the duplicate-id behavior correction, not just normative completion of r3.
- Consider engaging the ERC-8312 Ethereum Magicians thread with relevant findings from TAWG's bounded-action work.

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A hash-based challenge traveled the full loop in one window — from a discussion suggestion to benchmarked code to a commit in the living spec — while preflight discipline on the same ERC drew a clean line at the spec boundary before implementation could wander.
>
> The spec and the code are playing relay, not racing each other — and that's exactly when things actually ship. Keep the baton moving! 🏃
